title: Capturing Tail Outliers with Tail-Based Trace Sampling
prompt: A checkout platform processing 18,000 RPS uses 1% uniform head-based trace sampling to control APM ingestion costs ($14k/mo). Customers report intermittent 6-second freezes on 0.5% of orders, but APM shows almost zero slow traces because 99% of those rare outliers are dropped at the ingress gateway before the downstream lock contention even happens.

spark.summary: Uniform 1% head-based sampling drops 99% of slow and errored traces before they finish, leaving engineers blind to rare p99.9 latency outliers.
spark.keyTakeaway: When traffic spikes expose hidden coupling, switch from pure head-based probabilistic sampling to OpenTelemetry Collector tail-based sampling that buffers spans in memory for 30 s and keeps 100% of errors and high-latency traces.
spark.byteSummary:
**Core Mechanics:** At `18,000 RPS` (`12 spans/trace`, `~1.8 KB/span`), storing 100% of traces is cost-prohibitive, so teams enable `1%` uniform head-based sampling at ingress (`$14k/mo`).

**Visual & Structural Flow:** Depicts Trace-ID Consistent Hashing + 30s Memory Buffer Captures 100% Outliers (Services (18k RPS) -> L1 Trace-ID LB -> L2 Tail Collector -> APM (<1.2k/s)); Trace-ID Routing + 30s Decision Buffer + Policy Filter (L1 OTel LB + spanmetrics -> L2 Tail Buffer (30s) -> Policy Evaluator -> APM Storage (<1,200 spans/sec)).

**Trade-Offs & Production:** Two mistakes break naive tail-sampling rollouts: **Round-Robin Collector Fleet**: Without a Layer-1 `loadbalancing` exporter hashing `trace_id`, spans from Go/Java/Python scatter across pods, breaking trace assembly. Two-tier tail sampling is standard in high-throughput microservice observability: **Checkout & Payment Debugging**: Captures every rare third-party PSP timeout and lock-contention outlier.

learningJourney.title: Enterprise solution: Two-Tier OTel Tail-Sampling Pipeline

explanation.foundation: Capture `100%` of slow (`> 1,500 ms`) and errored traces while staying under `1,200 spans/sec` exported and `32 GB RAM/pod`:
explanation.core:
- **Layer 1 (`loadbalancing` Exporter)**: Receives `100%` of OTLP/gRPC spans (`388.8 MB/s`) and hashes `trace_id` so every span of a trace lands on the exact same Layer-2 collector pod.
- **Layer 2 (`tail_sampling` Processor, `decision_wait: 30s`)**: Buffers `30 s` of spans (`11.66 GB` raw, `~26 GB` total with Go overhead across e.g. 2–3 pods under `32 GB` each), then evaluates policies: keep `100%` of `latency > 1500ms` or `status == ERROR`, plus `0.5%` probabilistic baseline of fast traces.
- **Pre-Sampled Metrics (`spanmetrics`)**: Emit unsampled RED metrics at Layer 1 so SLO dashboards stay unbiased.
